operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are simple mixed-case (Classification, GeneID, Expression_Corr); no spaces, but case must be preserved and quoted.
Genes has NO primary key (pk=[]) yet GeneID is a FK to Classification and is 1:many (862 distinct over 4346 rows) — parent is unique, child is not.
Interactions has a composite PK (GeneID1, GeneID2) and TWO FKs to the SAME parent Classification(GeneID); both are self-consistent, no dangling.
FK graph: Classification (level 0) -> Genes, Interactions (level 1); no self-FK, no cycles, no missing parents.
GeneID values are text like 'G234064' (G + 6 digits); String fuzzer will treat them as int-like? No — leading 'G' means not int-like, so no +-1 variants.
Chromosome is INTEGER with only 17 distinct small values (1..17); Number fuzzer with scale=0 will draw huge ints in [-1,1] then perturb — mostly 0/1/-1.
Expression_Corr is REAL in [0,1] (samples 0.75..0.94); Number fuzzer scale=0 gives ints, not reals — storage class will contradict declared REAL.
Many TEXT columns are low-cardinality categoricals (Essential 4, Type 3, Phenotype 13, Function 13, Localization 15) with '?' as a sentinel value.
Complex is declared NULL-able but null_rate=0.0 in the sample; '?' used as missing sentinel instead.
All columns notnull=1 except Complex; no CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE indexes beyond PKs.
Tables are small (862/4346/910 rows) — no huge-table sampling concern; full read is fine.
No views, triggers, or indexes beyond PKs in DDL.
operator_ts_expectations: String fuzzer for all TEXT columns: fresh random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() of length 0..20, plus 5 sampled originals, plus contaminate (prefix/suffix/drop) — will produce garbage GeneIDs like 'aB3()' that break FK joins.

GeneID (String) fresh values won't match 'G\d{6}' pattern; FK consistency only holds when the child draws from the parent's generated values, so Genes.GeneID and Interactions.GeneID1/2 will be consistent with Classification.GeneID but implausible.
Number fuzzer for Chromosome (INTEGER, scale=0): range [-1,1], int perturb +-1/+-2 — will produce 0, -1, 2, etc., outside the real 1..17 domain.
Number fuzzer for Expression_Corr (REAL, scale=0): draws ints in [-1,1] with +-0.01/+-0.02 perturb — values like 0.99, -0.01, 1.02; storage becomes integer/real mix, contradicting REAL.

Low-cardinality categoricals (Essential, Type, Phenotype, Function, Localization, Class, Motif) get random strings, not the 3-24 real values — queries filtering 'Essential'='Essential' will return 0 rows (FN).
Genes has no PK, so sample_fresh_primary_keys is a no-op there; duplicate GeneID rows survive — but real data already has 1:many so this matches.
Interactions composite PK (GeneID1,GeneID2) dedup will drop rows; with random strings collisions are rare, so ~n rows kept.
FK child draws from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement — Genes.GeneID will be a random sample of Classification.GeneID (with dupes), preserving join cardinality roughly.
Known misses: FN from implausible categorical values (no 'Essential' rows), FP from missing ties (Expression_Corr random reals rarely tie, so ORDER BY / GROUP BY on it differs from gold).
Chromosome random ints rarely hit 1..17, so WHERE Chromosome=1 returns 0 rows (FN); but ties on Chromosome are plentiful (few distinct) — GROUP BY Chromosome may over-tie (FP).
No Date/Time/Bool columns — those fuzzers unused here.
